verdicts.notes: E4 kept: near-black navy base, far darker than every neighbour at 140, 200 and 320; fine dark swirl contours across the base and pale blue-white current streaks through it read as eerie currents (RM_Abyss_hard_140_crop.jpg). Soft and hard borders both read cleanly. B2 not grey mud: the patch is the darkest thing on the map, clearly apart from The Rot and desert around it.
E4 kept: wild-colour swirls (magenta, green, cyan, orange) flow continuously across tiles over a rich mottled purple texture, at 140, 200 and 320, soft and hard borders. Reads unlike any other biome.

E4 kept: a new hero face, not a restore: rust plates, girders, rivets and gears read as harsh rusty machinery at 140 and still read as a rust-machinery grid at 320; the grain (one gear-and-girder grid per several tiles) is far calmer than the fine speckle of the pre-calm face (RM_RustCathedral_face_precalm_calm_now.jpg: pre-calm, calm, now).

polish: Abyss: at 200 and above the pale currents are sparse (two or three streaks per ~127 tiles) and the vanilla hill glyphs on its mountainous tiles cover much of the base; a few more currents would make the 'eerie swirling' read from further out. Polish only: the promise reads at mid zoom.
Rust Cathedral: the gear-and-girder grid repeats on a visible square lattice over a large patch; a second variant or offset would hide the repeat once the paint makes the biome large. Polish only.
proposals: E2 (script-drawn stand-ins are no art) is written for sprites; world faces are drawn by biome_worldfaces.py by the owner's own route (this item's NEXT and card). The brief could say that procedurally generated world faces are art when an owner card orders them, so a later judge does not read E2 against them.
